cleared.result: Task 1, the rule as cycles/006/theme-currency-lists.work/census2.py applies it (cycle 18 and 19 census.py scripts are a different test: they replay sync and settle in callTracer frames, they do not balance flows). Inputs per block range: ERC-20 Transfer logs with the PoolManager as topic1 (out) or topic2 (in), counted only when the log has exactly three topics and 32 bytes of data (census2.py:69); WETH style Deposit(dst) logs naming the PoolManager, counted as in (census2.py:73-74); and every PoolManager log: Swap amounts as signed int128, Donate amounts, ModifyLiquidity pool ids, Initialize keys, and ERC-6909 Transfer logs with from = 0 (claims minted) or to = 0 (claims burned) (census2.py:76-91). Per transaction and currency: net = out + minted - in - burned; owed = sum of Swap amount0/amount1 of pools holding the currency, positive when the pool pays, minus Donate amounts (census2.py:106-111). A row is flagged only when net > owed and the transaction holds no ModifyLiquidity log of a pool with that currency (skipped-liquidity) and no pool event on a pool missing from the Initialize list (skipped-unknown-pool) (census2.py:118-123). Hook deltas have no event (src/PoolManager.sol:181, 224) and enter only through the Transfer and claim logs they cause; protocol fee collection has no event (src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57) and is recognised afterwards by rule.py from the trace (collectProtocolFees output) or from a fall of protocolFeesAccrued (cycles/006/theme-currency-lists.work/rule.py:171, 185). Native currency: a native transfer leaves no log, so a native row exists only when a claim of id 0 is minted or burned, or on Arc where 0xff..fe Transfer logs exist; on every other network such rows are counted as native-no-logs and skipped (census2.py:116). What the rule cannot see: (a) every native outflow on 20 of 21 networks; (b) any currency of a pool that has a ModifyLiquidity log in the same transaction, because the event carries liquidityDelta and no amounts (src/PoolManager.sol:175), so an outflow dressed as a liquidity removal or fee collection is never judged; (c) pools absent from the Initialize list; (d) a wrong amount that the PoolManager itself computes and logs: the Swap event is emitted from the same delta that is paid (src/PoolManager.sol:234-251), so an arithmetic fault in Pool.swap, SwapMath, SqrtPriceMath or FullMath that overpays a swapper is booked as owed and never flagged; this census therefore cannot test the opcode and integer library hypotheses of this cycle, which the mined swap replays in OPCODES.md test instead; (e) ERC-6909 transfers between accounts (from and to both nonzero, src/ERC6909.sol:30, 45), so claims moved from a victim and then burned for a take net to zero; (f) balance changes without a standard Transfer log, in either direction (rebases, mints that log only Deposit, tokens with nonstandard events); (g) freezes, which move nothing; (h) the flag is one sided: an inflow larger than owed is not reported.

leads.question: Can the census be widened to the transactions it skips: rows with a ModifyLiquidity in the same transaction (judge them by replaying Pool.modifyLiquidity from parent state and comparing principal plus fees with the outflow), native rows (judge by the PoolManager balance delta per transaction from a prestate trace), and ERC-6909 transfers between accounts?
leads.why: These three blind spots are the only paths by which a value leak that rides on a network difference could leave the PoolManager without the census flagging it; skipped-liquidity rows alone are 0.3 percent (X Layer) to 8.4 percent (Base) of the rows read this cycle.

leadResults.answer: Ink is now covered from deployment to head. On Base, Robinhood Chain, Ethereum and X Layer the newest contiguous range from the cycle 6 window to head and one oldest range from deployment are covered, with the gaps named in this unit. No transaction in the ranges read takes a currency out of the PoolManager without a pool event, a claim burn, a protocol fee collection or a recorded token class that pays for it. Ranges and gaps per network are in the cleared entries of this unit; Arbitrum One, OP Mainnet, Unichain and the remaining networks were not extended. The rule cannot see native outflows, liquidity removals or wrong amounts computed by the PoolManager, so it says nothing about arithmetic faults.

Ethereum F-104, F-071 and #1240 and Polygon F-072, #1180 and #1253 used publicnode logs, which cannot be tested now; F-104 and F-072 recount to the same numbers on tenderly, and the others cannot pass falsely on a missing log. F-091 and the cycle 6 BNB census used Pocket, which passes. F-112 used a keyed endpoint and stands on the cycle 18 test.
